title: Baked Spanish Omelette
subtitle: A hands-off oven version of the classic potato omelette that feeds a crowd
excerpt: A thick potato and egg omelette enriched with red pepper and finished in the oven, giving an even set throughout without the need to flip.
sourceNotes: A practical oven-baked take on the traditional Spanish tortilla, suited to feeding larger groups.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 days. Serve at room temperature.

glossaryTerms.definition: An omelette finished in the oven rather than flipped on the hob, giving an even set throughout.

content.text: This baked omelette serves 6 and takes 50 minutes in total. It starts on the hob to soften the vegetables and set the base, then transfers to the oven to finish evenly without any need to flip. The result is neater than a traditional tortilla and easier to scale for a bigger group.

Use an oven-safe frying pan so you can move it directly from hob to oven. If your pan has a plastic handle, wrap it in two layers of foil before putting it in the oven. Cook the potatoes gently in olive oil until completely tender before the egg goes in: any firmness at that stage will carry through to the finished omelette.

Heat the oven to 180C (fan 160C / Gas 4). Heat the olive oil in a 30cm oven-safe frying pan over a medium-low heat. Add the potato slices, onion and red pepper and cook gently for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are completely tender. Do not rush this step.
Drain off most of the oil, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan. Spread the vegetables in an even layer.
Beat the eggs well and season generously with black pepper. Pour the eggs over the vegetables in the pan. Lift the edges gently with a spatula so the egg runs underneath.
Cook on the hob for 3 minutes until the base is set and the edges are beginning to firm.
Transfer the pan to the oven and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the egg is fully set and the surface is lightly golden. A knife inserted in the centre should come out clean.
Leave to rest in the pan for 5 minutes, then slide onto a board or serve directly from the pan. Scatter with parsley if using. Cut into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

items.problem: The omelette is still wet in the centre after the stated time
items.solution: Return to the oven for 3 to 5 more minutes. Oven temperatures vary. Look for a set, barely-trembling centre rather than relying only on timing.

items.problem: The base is burnt but the top is still raw
items.solution: The hob was too hot before the oven stage. The base only needs 3 minutes on the hob; rely on the oven to do the rest.

items.problem: The potatoes are firm in the finished omelette
items.solution: They were not cooked through before the egg was added. Give them the full 20 minutes on a gentle heat. A fork should pass through with no resistance.

that removes the anxiety of the flip. It is as at home on a picnic blanket as it is at a table. The red pepper adds sweetness and colour that the classic version lacks. It keeps well in the fridge and is arguably better the next day, eaten cold in thick slices.
